issues.body: In `queue_topic_changes`, a deleted topic is checked with `allowed(auth_anchor(topic), Read)`. After deletion, `auth_anchor` falls back to the nearest existing ancestor. If the subscriber previously lost read access through a resource-specific ACL but can read that ancestor, a later delete is delivered even though the session may no longer read the subscribed resource. This contradicts the documented delivery-time re-check and leaks the resource's deletion. The current revocation test covers a still-existing container only, so it does not exercise this path.
issues.fix_hint: Snapshot each subscribed topic's read authorization before the mutation as well as its digest. For a Delete transition, require that the topic was readable immediately before deletion and that the post-mutation governing authorization permits disclosure; do not substitute ancestor readability alone for the topic's lost policy. Add a regression test where a child-specific ACL revokes read while the parent remains readable, then the child is deleted, and assert that no notification is queued.
issues.title: Delete notifications can bypass resource-specific read revocation

verdict.summary: The resources surface and its tests are substantial, but deletion delivery does not actually enforce the claimed per-delivery authorization for the subscribed resource. Once the resource is removed, the implementation authorizes against an ancestor instead; that can re-authorize a session whose resource-specific read access had already been revoked and leak that the resource was deleted.
